subject: Game Theory
title: The Trust Game
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Trust Game.

hook.text: You're given $10. You can send any amount to a stranger. It triples. They decide how much to return.

buildup.text: Rational self-interest says: send nothing, because the stranger should keep everything. Most people send.

discovery.text: Experiments show people send about half, and recipients return enough to reward trust. Humans aren't selfish.

twist.text: Oxytocin levels predict trust: people given synthetic oxytocin send 17% more money to strangers.

climax.text: Paul Zak's research showed trust is partly biological—our brains are wired for social bonding, not just greed.

punchline.text: Trust is the currency of cooperation.

quiz.question: What do trust game experiments reveal?
options: Most people show and reciprocate trust
